title: Health Safety
intro: Travel Medicine Clinic: Make appointment June–July 2026; bring your itinerary; update based on current CDC travel health notices at [travel.cdc.gov](https://travel.cdc.gov).

tables.caption: Vaccinations (visit travel medicine clinic 6–8 weeks before departure)
rows: Food and water-borne; applies to both countries
Street food consumption in both countries
Mosquito-borne; rural Vietnam (My Son); Sept is active season
September = start of flu season in Asia
No entry requirement but healthcare exposure risk
Neither China nor Vietnam is a Yellow Fever risk country or requires proof
Only if planning extended contact with animals; not needed for this itinerary
Beijing: zero risk; Hanoi/Đà Nẵng: negligible urban risk; My Son: minimal

tables.caption: First Aid Kit
rows: 1 pair (for boat trip to Cham Islands)
Beijing United Family Hospital (和睦家医院)
International standard; English-speaking staff; works with foreign insurance
Peking Union Medical College Hospital (协和医院)
Top Chinese hospital; less English; can use for emergencies
Best international-standard hospital in Hanoi; English staff; +84-24-3974-3556
Western-staffed GP clinic; good for non-emergency; +84-24-3843-0748
C Hospital Đà Nẵng (Bệnh viện C)
Main city hospital; crowded; less English
For minor issues; call resort reception; doctor can come to room

tables.caption: Beijing Safety
rows: Wallet in front pocket; camera strap around wrist; standard vigilance
Tea ceremony scam (young woman invites you for tea → ¥2,000+ bill); art gallery scam; English student scam — decline all impromptu invitations
Look right THEN left at crossings; electric scooters run silently on sidewalks
Don't engage in political conversations; don't photograph military installations

tables.caption: Vietnam Safety (Hanoi + Đà Nẵng/Hội An)
rows: Don't walk with phone/purse dangling from shoulder near streets; motorbikes can snatch
Negotiate; know approximate prices; have small bills ready
Monitor weather; resort is your shelter; see 16-contingency
Walk at steady pace; motorbikes flow around you

tables.caption: Document Backup Protocol
rows: Saved in email + saved in Notes app
Credit card numbers + bank phone numbers
Write on paper in secured luggage

bullets.heading: Pre-Trip Health
items: Medical evacuation (China: medical care for foreigners is expensive and evacuation to Hong Kong or home may be necessary in serious cases)
Trip cancellation for typhoon (Vietnam leg)
Pre-existing conditions waiver
Activity coverage: hiking (Great Wall), snorkeling (Cham Islands), water activities
Baggage loss
World Nomads (worldnomads.com): Standard Explorer plan; covers adventure activities; medical evacuation included
Allianz Travel: OneTrip Prime; good medical limits; widely recognized in Asia
Purchase: Same day as first flight booking to activate pre-departure cancellation coverage
Bring sufficient supply for entire 14 days + 3 extra days buffer
Original prescription from doctor + note in English (for customs)
Controlled substances: Check SAMHSA list against China and Vietnam regulations — common anxiety medications and some sleep aids face import restrictions
Anti-diarrheal (Imodium) + oral rehydration salts: Pack in carry-on
Altitude sickness: Not relevant for this route (all cities are at sea level or low elevation)

bullets.heading: Health Per Country
items: GI issues (food/water adjustment) — most common; resolved with Imodium + hydration
Jet lag — 12–13 hr time difference from US East; allow Day 1 for adjustment
Sunburn — September sun in Beijing is still strong; apply SPF 50 daily

bullets.heading: Emergency Protocol Per Country
items: Beijing: 55 An Jia Lou Rd; +86-10-8531-4000 (24/7 emergency)
Hanoi: 7 Lang Ha, Ba Dinh; +84-24-3850-5000 (24/7 emergency)
Register trip: [travel.state.gov/STEP](https://travel.state.gov/STEP) — receive emergency notifications
